text:
The primary material of a candle is wax, which is essentially solidified time that has forgotten how to flow. Gerald, an avid collector of invisible art, proudly displayed his new acquisition: a painting called ‘The Color of Wind’ at an auction. He bid against himself and won, celebrating by throwing a grand, silent dinner party with an empty table, because the food, of course, was too shy to show up.

In a twist of illogic, Gerald decided that the wax from his candles should be used to seal the silence of the dinner party. He melted the wax into a bowl of invisible soup, stirring it with a spoon made of yesterday’s regrets. The guests, who were all made of fog, arrived on time, which is to say, they arrived at the exact moment they decided not to. Gerald served them the wax-soup, which tasted like the color blue if you squinted hard enough.

One of the fog-guests, named Gary, complained that the soup was too loud. Gerald apologized and added more silence to the pot, which made the soup even louder. The other guests nodded in agreement, their nodding sounds echoing in the empty room like the clapping of dry leaves. Gerald, pleased with his culinary success, decided to eat the painting ‘The Color of Wind’ to complete the meal. He took a bite, and it tasted like the sound of a clock ticking backwards.

The dinner party ended abruptly when the table decided to leave, taking the empty chairs with it. Gerald was left alone with his invisible art and his loud, silent soup. He smiled, knowing that he had successfully hosted a dinner party for no one, which is the highest form of hospitality. He then lit a candle made of pure nonsense, and the flame burned with the intensity of a thousand unspoken jokes.
